Subject: Observability onboarding: dashboards, traces, and alert routing

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. This thread is to lock down our initial operational checklist and owners so the implementation sprint can start next week. High-level goals for the onboarding phase:

- Deliver a set of three production dashboards (latency, error breakdown, token cost)
- Add tracing hooks for the request lifecycle (inference request -> model selection -> runtime kernel)
- Define an error taxonomy and map to alert routing/runbooks
- Hand off runbook ownership to your SRE on go-live

Proposed schedule (UTC-8):
1) Nov 23 — kick-off workshop (60m): architecture review + access checks
2) Nov 24–26 — instrumentation pass (traces + logs)
3) Nov 29 — dashboard review + alert thresholds
4) Dec 1 — production handover and runbook sign-off

Action items I want to confirm from your side before the kickoff:
- A small SRE contact who will own runbook signoff (name + email)
- An example request id (or test dataset) so we can validate traces end-to-end
- Any regulatory retention constraints for logs/metrics (90/180/other days)

I've attached a short onboarding checklist and a sample trace span schema we recommend. I'll loop Ben (CS lead) and Laura (implementation) into the thread for the technical details.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Evan / team — short technical checklist from CS side before we start:

1) Tracing ingestion
- We'll accept x-bluewave-trace-id and x-bw-span; please send a snippet of how you generate spans (trace id format and parent/child semantics). If you can paste a single example HTTP payload, we can validate parsing.

2) Span attributes we expect (min):
- request.id, customer.id, model.name, model.variant, sequence.length, runtime.node_id

3) Dashboard targets
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) by model.variant
- Error taxonomy counts (client_error / model_error / infra_error)
- Per-customer token spend and request volume (daily)

4) Alert routing
- Severity mapping: Sev0 (platform down) -> SRE pager; Sev1 (model regression, spike) -> SRE + CS; Sev2 (configuration/cost threshold) -> CS only
- We need a primary and secondary pager contact for Sev0/Sev1.

5) Access
- Please create a staging API key (read-only telemetry) and grant redwood-staging@bluewave the following IAM roles or a similar token we can use to pull traces in staging.

If you prefer, Laura and I can do a 30m run through of your current tracer implementation after the kickoff.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Hi all —

Short answer on rollback/fallback:
- Automatic fallback: We configure a model-variant fallback policy tied to alert rules. If model_error rate > X% for Y minutes, traffic is redirected to a pre-defined compatible variant (read-only on the policy).
- Manual rollback: Priya (BlueWave SRE) or Redwood SRE on-call can initiate a manual rollback in the console. We'll add the exact runbook steps to the runbook-template.md and mark the runbook owner field for Priya to sign off during final handover.

Next steps I will own before Nov 29:
- Create three dashboard drafts in the shared Drive (links posted in drive folder)
- Add alert policy stubs for Sev0/Sev1/Sev2 and set default thresholds (we'll test in staging)
- Populate the runbook template with the rollback steps, paging escalation, and the contact matrix (Priya -> Marcus -> Redwood SRE)

I created JIRA ticket OPS-4821 for the instrumentation work and linked it to this deal. Priya — when you grant the staging key, I'll pick one example trace and post a sample trace screenshot to the Drive folder so the dashboards can reference real data.

Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
